1.why: Every MFA endpoint derives state via mfa(s.accountId) from the server-side session record, so settings are always scoped to the signed-in account and no client-supplied user identifier is accepted.

2.why: Identity challenge codes are random per-challenge and bound to the challenge cookie, identityKey and accountId with constant-time ownership checks, so a code cannot be reused for another user; only the static TEST_MODE mock code is shared, and even it requires an existing matching identity.

3.why: The /api/mfa/verify-otp handler sets v.enabled = true but never deletes or re-issues the session record or cookie, so the session established before enrolment remains valid afterwards.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext with a random IV and backup codes are stored as PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations, per-code salt) hashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, session/CSRF tokens, digits, base32 seeds and recovery codes are produced from crypto.getRandomValues, with rejection sampling in digit() to avoid modulo bias.

6.why: Session and challenge cookies use __Host- prefix with HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict and nothing is written to localStorage/sessionStorage; only transient in-memory JS variables and the demo log panel hold the secret and backup codes.

7.why: Server-side validators emailOK, phoneOK, otpOK, recoveryInput plus normalisation and a ROUTES allow-list for redirect reject malformed input before use, and there is no SQL/data store to inject into (in-memory Maps).

8.why: All dynamic values (manual secret, backup codes, logs, headings) are injected with textContent/createElement rather than innerHTML, and the server returns JSON only, so injected markup cannot execute.

9.why: The redirect field is validated against the fixed ROUTES set server-side and client navigation only uses hash routes filtered through the same whitelist, with no Location header built from user input.

10.why: secureHeaders sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie/challengeCookie/clearCookie all emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Path=/ and the __Host- prefix.

12.why: Server errors are generic ("The request could not be completed.") with no stack traces or secrets in URLs, but the client deliberately console.logs and renders the manual TOTP secret, mock codes and every newly issued backup recovery code into a visible Logs panel.

13.why: Identity challenges are marked used and deleted with a 2-minute expiry, provisioning expires in 5 minutes and the accepted counter blocks TOTP replay; the only weakness is the fixed TEST_MODE mock codes which never expire while test mode is on.

14.why: identityAttempts, otpAttempts and recoveryAttempts all use failed()/isLocked() to lock out for 10 minutes after 5 failures, returning 429.

15.why: Sign-in deletes any pre-existing session cookie and mints a new random session id and CSRF token, getSession enforces a 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and logout deletes the server record and clears the cookie.
